'''Lance Alan Mehl''' (born February 14, 1958) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for eight seasons with the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), from 1980 to 1987. He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. Mehl was selected by the Jets in the third round of the [[1980 NFL draft]] with the 69th overall pick. He was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] in 1985.

Mehl was the leading [[Tackle (football move)|tackler]] for the unbeaten 1978 Nittany Lion team. He earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Industrial Arts Education from Penn State University in 1980.

Mehl was a three-sport [[team captain]] at [[Bellaire High School (Ohio)|Bellaire High School]] in [[Bellaire, Ohio]] in [[High school football|football]], [[baseball]], and [[basketball]].

Today, Mehl is retired from working to help troubled youth. He is the father of four sons: Lance Jr, Lucas, Logan, and Layne. Lance's mother was Beulah.

According to Lance Mehl's 1984 Topps football card #153, he was the Jets leading interceptor in 1983. He recorded 10 tackles in 44-17 playoff win at Cincinnati Jan 9, 1983. As a bit of "Did You Know" the card said "Lance once worked in the coal mines of Ohio"  In 1985, he was selected to play in the Pro Bowl.

Mehl wore the number #56 while playing for the New York Jets.

In 2012,  Mehl testified as a character witness on behalf of former coach [[Jerry Sandusky]], calling him, "a class act."  However, in a later interview, he said, "no doubt, if coach Sandusky is truly guilty of these crimes, he must be punished...and punished severely."<ref>{{cite web|last=Gibson|first=Rich|title=Sandusky scandal continues to haunt former Lion Mehl|url=http://www.timesleaderonline.com/page/content.detail/id/539444/Sandusky-scandal-continues-to-haunt-former-Lion-Mehl.html|work=Times Leader Online|accessdate=7 December 2013}}</ref> Sandusky was later found guilty of 45 felony charges related to child rape and child endangerment.

'''Lamar Hunter Smith''' (born November 29, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[New Orleans Saints]], and [[Carolina Panthers]] from 1994 to 2003. He played [[college football]] for the [[Houston Cougars football|Houston Cougars]] and was selected by Seattle in the third round of the [[1994 NFL draft]].

On December 30, 2000, Smith carried the ball a then-NFL record 40 times for the Dolphins in a [[Wild card (sports)|wildcard]] playoff game against the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He finished with 209 yards rushing, including a 17-yard touchdown run in overtime to give the Dolphins a 23–17 victory, Miami's most recent playoff victory as of the 2025 season.{{Citation needed|date=March 2024}}

'''Lamonte Hunley''' (born January 31, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1985 to 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HunlLa20.htm |title=Lamonte Hunley Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=2018-11-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/lamontehunley/2517046/profile |title=Lamonte Hunley, LB |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=2018-11-24}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats football|Arizona Wildcats]], whose teammates included his older brother, [[Ricky Hunley|Ricky]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/129696864|title=Oh brother: Move has Lamonte Hunley following in footsteps of Ricky|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Bob|last=Nightengale|date=August 22, 1984|access-date=August 8, 2023|page=81|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Prior to his senior season, Hunley was moved from weakside inside linebacker to strongside inside linebacker, following in his brother's footsteps.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/129771356|title=Hunley adjusting to new job|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|first=Rich|last=Dymond|date=August 28, 1984|access-date=August 8, 2023|page=9|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref name="Tucs841123">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/129776554|title=Lamonte Hunley made strongside case for self|work=[[Tucson Citizen]]|first=Dave|last=Petruska|date=November 23, 1984|access-date=August 8, 2023|pages=1E, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/129776778 4E]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Hunley earned first-team All-[[Pac-10 Conference]] honors in his new role.{{r|Tucs841123}}

After going undrafted in the [[1985 NFL draft]], Hunley signed a [[free agent]] contract with the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. As a rookie, he recorded 25 special teams tackles, which ranked second on the team.<ref name="star">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/129777486|title=Hunley hopes to fill Krauss' shoes|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|first=Mike|last=Chappell|date=October 3, 1986|access-date=August 8, 2023|page=31|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Hunley earned playing time at right inside linebacker in 1986 after the team's leading tackler, [[Barry Krauss]], suffered a season-ending against the [[New York Jets]].<ref name=star/> Hunley recorded five solo tackles, one assisted tackle, and one fumble recovery in the game.<ref name=star/> However, he suffered a foot injury a few weeks later and was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].

After his playing career, Hunley became a co-owner of Arizona Health, a fitness equipment store, along with partner Scott Thompson.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/129777173|title=They're going strong|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|first=Djamila|last=Grossman|date=April 13, 2006|access-date=August 8, 2023|page=150|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
